'''Christian Jung''' (born 17 September 1956, [[Northeim]], [[Lower Saxony]]), is a plant geneticist and molecular biologist in the Plant Breeding Institute<ref name = breding>{{cite web | title = Plant Breeding Institute|url = https://www.plantbreeding.uni-kiel.de/}}</ref> of [[Kiel University]].<ref name = breeding>{{cite web | url = https://www.plantbreeding.uni-kiel.de/de/Staff/prof.-dr.-christian-jung | title = Prof. Dr. Christian Jung}}</ref>

== Career ==

After internships in agricultural companies in Germany and Canada Jung studied at the [[University of Göttingen]] with Hans Günter Schlegel, and in 1981 obtained a diploma on the basis of the "Detection of nitrogen fixation in two strains of the hydrogen bacterium ''Alcaligenes latus''".<ref name = breeding/> He  studied at the Institute for Plant Production and Plant Breeding of the same university, where he received his doctorate in 1984 with a thesis on the "Intrinsic performance and interactions of rye and wheat genomes in triticale" supervised by Gerhard Röbbelen.<ref name = breeding/>

Later Jung had positions at the [[Leibniz University Hannover]]<ref name = breeding/> and [[LMU Munich]]<ref name = breeding/> before becoming Professor and Director at 
the Plant Breeding Institute of Kiel University.<ref name = breeding/>

==Research==
Jung's principal interest is in molecular breeding and the development of pest-resistant crops. In that respect he is known for cloning a resistance gene against nematodes in beets.<ref>{{cite journal | doi= 10.1126/science.275.5301.832| title = Positional cloning of a gene for nematode resistance in sugar beet

==Awards==
